newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Cable & Wireless posts strong half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Cable & Wireless posts strong half.

text.p: British telecommunications company Cable & Wireless Plc on Wednesday posted a nine percent rise in underlying profits for the first half of the year, beating most analysts' estimates.
C&W said first-half pretax profits, excluding exceptional items, rose to 673 million pounds ($1.13 billion) -- above analyst estimates of 650 to 668 million pounds.
The company, which recently concluded a major alliance with British cable operators, raised its interim dividend to 3.4 pence per share from 3.08 pence in the year-ago period.

"We have delivered a strong competitive performance during the first half, and I remain confident about the outlook," chief executive Richard Brown said in his first results statement since he took over the post earlier this year.
Turnover, including the firm's share in associates, rose 14 percent to 3.40 billion pounds, while group operating margins increased to 25 percent from 23.
Despite the higher-than-expected results, C&W's shares dipped 0.5 pence to 482.5 by midday after hitting 490 earlier in an overall weaker London market.
In an interview, Brown said Cable & Wireless had talked with U.S.-based NYNEX Corp and other firms about possible new alliances.
However, he emphasised the company felt no need to align itself with one partner.
"I would characterise them as good business discussions," he said of the talks. "Where other companies have brought us opportunities to look at, we are responding to those ideas."

C&W's plan to merge its Mercury unit with three British cable operators, including NYNEX CableComms Group, fuelled rumours it might seek to expand its alliance with NYNEX beyond the new company, called Cable & Wireless Communications.

"We would not limit what we may choose to do to just Cable and Wireless Communications," Brown said. "We are talking beyond that, but I don't want to mislead you and have you believe they're the only company of any major scale we're talking to, because it's not."

"(This is) not to imply that there's some lock-up here that's imminent," he added. "That's not true at all. I have said we are large enough to be successfully independent and small enough to be nimble."

He declined to identify the other companies Cable & Wireless had talked to, but added: "I would say probably the only one we haven't seriously talked to is MCI with BT. We've left the door wide open for anybody interested to come and talk with us."

Brown added that Cable & Wireless was well positioned to compete with the new company formed by the planned $20 billion merger of British Telecommunications Plc and U.S.-based MCI Communications Corp.
"Just because you're bigger doesn't make you better," he said. C&W's own merger talks with BT broke down in May.

Brown said the firm's directly-connected customer lines in Britain rose 16 percent in the first half. Operating margins at Mercury improved to 16 percent from 12 percent, while underlying revenue growth was six percent.

The half-year results excluded an exceptional profit of 61 million pounds on C&W's sale of part of its stake in Asia Satellite Telecommunication Holdings Ltd, and a gain last year of 199 million pounds on the sale of its stake in Germany's Mannesmann Mobilfunk.
Including exceptionals, the company's pretax profits fell to 734 million pounds from 815 million a year ago. ($1=.5970 Pound)
